title: Missing home, a granddaughter's birth and advice about going to Europe
summary: Howard would go again; news of a granddaughter in London; why local musicians hesitate; tiring concerts.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Did you miss New Orleans very much?

No, I'm afraid I didn't. At first I did because at that time when we was, came back to Liverpool when we was making a tour all over Europe. We came back to London when I was to water up at my daughter. That's right. And the night on the stage we was doing a concert, we got a telegram that she had a little baby girl and after that everything was fine.
Yeah, but love said it all about that.

I've noticed that in corresponding with different musicians here in New Orleans, I asked them if they would like to go to Europe on tour because I know that sometimes there has maybe more work to be found there than there is around here at the moment, that they don't seem to be too keen on leaving the city here.
And they're just a little scared of what might be ahead of them when they... Well, I don't see why they should. Do you think it's because they don't know so much about Europe? They don't...
Well, probably they haven't talked to the right people. Those that I talked to, I explained to them the best I knew and tell them exactly the absolute thanks. Yeah.
Do you find it hard and tiring to work in those concerts in Europe? It's always very big halls and...

Well, no, because you get your breaks. Well, the only thing, well, you'd expect that, is when you get the breaks you have the autographs and this and talk to that one or two at that time, and you're supposed to get a rest, which you don't. You know. That's in the game. Did you know that New Orleans jazz was so popular in Europe? I didn't. And that people really started it then? I was surprised when I heard the fellas play so wonderful.
